elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The access and right to use granted to the Company under this Section 1.4 shall extend to the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI" — affiliates are covered, albeit conditioned on notice.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 1.4 as rendered nor the inserted sentence mentions contractors or agents acting on the Company's behalf; only affiliates were added.
No perpetuity language anywhere in the rendered Section 1.4; the grant of access/use rights carries no stated duration or 'perpetual' qualifier.
The rendered text contains no 'irrevocable' wording; absence of an express at-will revocation right is not an affirmative irrevocability commitment.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Section 1.4 as amended says nothing about the grounds for terminating or suspending the access/use rights; no 'only for uncured material breach' limitation was added.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The insertion permits transfer only "to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction" — the narrower fallback formulation, not general transferability to Customer's successors (e.g. by reorganisation or asset sale).

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "shall extend to the Company's affiliates upon written notice to HDI" — expressly ties affiliate coverage to written notice, exactly the fallback mechanic.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "and may be transferred by the Company to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction." — Customer-side transfer right, correct party direction and trigger.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: one inserted sentence delivers both affiliate coverage on written notice and M&A successor transferability in operative language, not merely in the margin comment.

Preferred level fails on four counts — no contractors, no perpetual, no irrevocable, no 'terminable only for uncured material breach' — and the successor transfer is limited to M&A rather than successors generally. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add "and to contractors acting on the Company's behalf", state that the rights are perpetual and irrevocable once fees are paid, restrict termination of the rights to uncured material breach, and broaden the transfer right to any successor.

Minimality holds: the original Section 1.4 wording is retained verbatim, nothing was deleted or paraphrased, and the addition contains no extras (no survival tail, no expense or procedure language, no requirements outside the fallback checklist).

Intent preserved: the insertion is scoped expressly to "this Section 1.4", leaves the hosting/bandwidth and Content-administration mechanics untouched, and creates no contradiction with the Section 10.3 successors-and-assigns clause or any other retained sentence; no dangling cross-reference is introduced.

Minor note for the rationale rather than a defect: "affiliates" is not a defined term in the agreement, so the drafter may wish to add a short definition or use the counterparty's customary formulation if HDI pushes back.
